title: Chicken Cacciatore
description: A hearty Italian classic — tender chicken simmered in a rich tomato and olive sauce, perfect over jasmine rice.

method.instruction: Heat 30 ml of olive oil in a large deep pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Brown chicken on both sides, about 3–4 minutes per side, until golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add remaining 15 ml of oil. Add chopped onion and sauté for 2–3 minutes until softened.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the white wine and vinegar. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2–3 minutes to reduce slightly.
Crumble in the stock cubes and add hot water. Stir to dissolve.
Add the tomatoes, crushing them with your hands or a spoon, along with basil and sugar. Stir well.
Return the browned chicken to the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 25–30 minutes until chicken is cooked through and tender.
Add Kalamata olives and milk. Stir gently and simmer uncovered for another 5–7 minutes to let the sauce thicken slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Stir in chopped parsley just before serving.
Serve hot over jasmine rice, pasta, or with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.

notes.title: Wine and Vinegar Balance
notes.content: Adjust wine and vinegar to taste for tanginess. Start with less and add more if you prefer a sharper flavour.

notes.title: Chicken Thighs
notes.content: Chicken thighs can be used instead of breasts for extra juiciness and flavour. Bone-in thighs will need 10–15 minutes longer cooking time.

notes.title: Reheating
notes.content: This dish tastes even better the next day as the flavours develop. Reheat gently on the stovetop.

notes.title: Recipe Origin
notes.content: Adapted from traditional Italian cacciatore recipes — a classic hunter-style braise.
